doc.title: Nancy Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, November 16, 1995

chapter: Coming to New York and signing
title: Choosing John Levy, Capitol and a career plan
summary: She wanted a manager who cared for her as a person, and aimed for Capitol Records, David Cavanaugh and MCA; she arrived in New York in 1959 as Cannonball was ill.

story.theme_name: Playing with and around Miles Davis

blocks.x: What a rare commodity — to have a musician, a fine musician, who would step into that role. “I want to be with him.”

That you know would care about you as a person as opposed to being in the “show business” mode. I did not have this great desire to be in show business, so I really needed to know that there was somebody out there who would allow me to be a person and to use the music to enhance, but be a part of, as opposed to just overshadow everything else. And John understood that. We met, his assistant was a young man from Ohio, Chuck Taylor. As I say, I met Cannon on the corner, this is when he and Nat, in fact both he and Nat were in New York for one of the first times. This was about the time that Julian [Cannonball] was, they were disbanding their first group, Cannon was going with Miles and Nat was going with Lionel Hampton. So we were, we became friends. We talked, we exchanged numbers. And Cannonball told John, Chuck Taylor had already told John, John Levy was very much aware for several years before I ever got to New York that there is this kid in Columbus, Ohio who sings. So it was kind of, it worked, I mean all of it worked out nicely. I’m just grateful that I was not the kind of person who put the cart before the horse and wanted it to happen all of a sudden. I needed to know me before I wanted to do this. And I figured that if I got to know who I was and put happiness in perspective and knew what it meant to be happy, then I could handle this business. And I could do that with John Levy. I also wanted Capitol Records. I thought David Cavanaugh was one of the best producers. He produced Nat Cole and Peggy Lee, Dakota Staton, Jonah Jones. Because everybody out there — Capitol Records was the singer’s label. Johnny Mercer was there. I mean who, what could be better? So I shot for and I wanted that. I wanted MCA which was the biggest agency. I wanted to play supper clubs, I wanted the Coconut Grove as opposed to Sawdust, because I’m going to give this my time and my effort. If I’m going to do it I want it to be right. And John understood that. We talked and when I finally did come to New York, it was at the same week that Julian was first diagnosed and these illnesses were discovered. I was 22. It was in 1959. And when I arrived in New York, Cannonball was in the hospital. And we talked and he was able to go back out and did many, many things. I ran into him in Ohio, obviously, when he was with Miles.
